free_tier.stated: 50 GB per transfer, all files combined, no account required. Hosted in Infomaniak's own Swiss datacentres. One notable global property: the source is open (Infomaniak android/iOS/multiplatform clients on GitHub) and there is a working CLI.

retention.stated: Retention: 15 days by default; 30 only if the SENDER accepts an extension email on day 12 (offer open 3 days)

egress.terms: Unmetered, no egress pricing published; direct download links plus a 'Download All' ZIP (ZIP is capped. Above 10 GB you must fetch files one by one).

record.tooling: Swissfer (github.com/Blutsh/swissfer, 44 stars, pushed 2026-10-21). Rust CLI, upload AND download, email-confirmed sender. First upload requires a 6-character code emailed to you, then cached. Upstream `send`-style clients do not work.
record.chaining: Per-transfer 50 GB x unlimited transfers. With swissfer this is scriptable, so capacity is bounded by how many 50 GB transfers you are willing to mint, each living 15-30 days.
record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: 50 GB per transfer (combined, not per file). Retention: 15 days by default; 30 only if the SENDER accepts an extension email on day 12 (offer open 3 days). After expiry Infomaniak states a link cannot be reactivated or extended. pull-count: download cap selectable at 1/20/100/250. 'unlimited' requires a paid plan. Request-rate: the container-create endpoint enforces a reCAPTCHA field (see reliability note).
record.reliability_note: The write path requires human verification at the API: POST /api/containers without a recaptcha field returns 400 'The recaptcha field is required. (and 1 more error)'. swissfer routes around this with an emailed 6-char confirmation, not with a token. The 30-day option is a trap. It silently deletes at 15 days unless the sender acts on day 12.

evidence.proved: '50 GB', retention table, download caps, 'cannot be reactivated or extended'
